summary: VXLAN + WAN MSS clamping causes TLS record reassembly mismatch and large shard range failures on private deploy
summary_short: Large shard range downloads intermittently fail with 416/502 behind VXLAN + WAN optimizer
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent failures retrieving large model shard byte-ranges (presigned range GETs) from S3-backed artifact storage after migrating a subset of serving nodes onto an on-prem edge that uses VXLAN overlay and a WAN optimizer that clamps TCP MSS. Errors observed: 416 Range Not Satisfiable and occasional 502 from the serving node during range assembly.

Impact:
- Several inference requests for large models fail intermittently for AuroraHealth private deployment.
- Affected routes show increased retries and token-level cost spikes due to re-fetch attempts.
- Customer reports degraded user experience for batch-generation jobs during nightly windows.

Environment:
- Private deployment (customer-managed VPC + on-prem edge)
- us-east-1 region egress through Direct Connect to customer WAN appliance (VXLAN overlay)
- Serving nodes run runtime v1.9.4; artifact downloader component v2.3.1
- Observed on a subset of nodes pinned to AZ1 behind the customer's SD-WAN

Steps to reproduce:
1. Deploy a large model (>1.5GB) with sharded artifacts and presigned range URLs.
2. From a serving node routed through the customer's VXLAN overlay and WAN optimizer, initiate concurrent presigned range GETs with byte ranges > 64KB per request.
3. Observe retries and intermittent 416/502 responses; put a tcpdump on the host to capture TLS records and IP fragmentation behavior.

Observed behavior:
- S3 returns valid ETag and Accept-Ranges; however the serving node logs show mismatched Content-Range assembly and range validation failures leading to 416 or downstream 502 when reassembling shards.
- Packet captures show TCP MSS clamped to ~1200 bytes by WAN optimizer and VXLAN adding 50+ bytes of encapsulation, resulting in TLS records being split across multiple IP fragments and reordering under ECMP.

Expected behavior:
- Large range GETs should stream and reassemble into correct byte ranges regardless of MTU/VXLAN encapsulation. Serving node should tolerate smaller MSS without producing range validation errors.

Attachments/Artifacts:
- pcap snippets from customer host (redacted)
- serving node error logs (range-validator WARN/ERROR)
- CloudFront/S3 GET logs showing range requests and 206/200 responses
- Console dashboard screenshots showing increased retry rate and token cost spike
steps_to_reproduce: Deploy large sharded model (>1.5GB) with presigned range URLs
Route serving nodes through VXLAN overlay + WAN optimizer with MSS clamping enabled
Send concurrent range GETs with ranges >64KB and capture packets and logs
logs_and_metrics: serving-node: range-validator ERROR: expected 1048576-2097151 but received bytes 1048576-2098688
s3: 206 Partial Content for range bytes=1048576-...
tcpdump: IP frag offset non-zero; TLS record split across fragments
cloudwatch: artifact-download latency 95p increased from 120ms to 1.4s
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: PMTU/MSS clamping is fragmenting TLS records inside VXLAN which combined with ECMP reordering leads to record reassembly mismatches in artifact downloader
Reproduced locally by forcing MSS to 1200 and enabling VXLAN encapsulation; observed identical range mismatch errors
Checked serving-runtime code: range-validator assumes contiguous TLS application data per read; it does not currently tolerate mid-record reassembly delays beyond stream-level timeouts
Customer confirmed WAN optimizer performs MSS clamp to 1200 and also reorders flows when under load
comments: Support (Maya Chen) - 2026-03-10: Initial triage: asked for pcaps, serving node logs, and exact azs/nodes affected.
Customer (AuroraHealth - N. Ramirez) - 2026-03-10: Uploaded pcaps and confirmed appliance vendor (RiverGate WAN) clamps MSS to 1200 on egress when encryption overlay is active.
Eng (Luca Ferrara) - 2026-03-11: Verified reproduction in lab by emulating VXLAN + MSS 1200. Attached demo capture. Proposing short-term workarounds and longer-term code fix.
Support (Maya Chen) - 2026-03-11: Provided customer workaround steps to set artifact downloader to use smaller range chunk sizes and increase read timeouts.
Customer (N. Ramirez) - 2026-03-12: Workaround reduced incidence from 7% to ~0.5% during nightly batches; customer requests timeline for permanent fix.
short_term_workaround: Lower artifact downloader range chunk size to 32KB and increase stream reassembly timeout on affected serving nodes. Disable concurrent range merging at downloader layer behind VXLAN until fix deployed.
long_term_resolution_plan: Engineering to implement TLS-aware range reassembly in artifact downloader: buffer partial TLS records across reads and validate byte-range assembly independent of transport MTU fragmentation. Also add an auto-detect for MTU/MSS and adapt range chunk size at runtime. Target patch in serving-runtime v1.9.6.
resolution: In progress - customer accepted short-term workaround; engineering assigned to code change with ETA 2026-03-25 for canary. Will track rollout and post-deploy validation.
